| [QUESTION-245](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-245.md) | For linear decisions at the population level, if a kind's admissible transformations are given as a distribution over pairs of its realizations, is the top eigenspace of the pair operator a stable, decision-sufficient span, and what span takes that role when the pairs are directed? | The linear part of [QUESTION-052](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-052.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). For symmetric pairs, yes: the top eigenfunctions are the most view-invariant directions, and their span is minimax-optimal for linear prediction of approximately view-invariant targets ([THEORY-007](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-007.md)) and bounds linear-probe error by leakage over conductance ([THEORY-228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-228.md)). For directed pairs, the top left singular functions of the conditional-expectation operator take that role ([THEORY-239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md)), and a linear readout of the full density ratio suffices for redundant labels ([THEORY-319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md)). Other spans can tie. Nonlinear decisions, and what picks one signature out, stay with [QUESTION-052](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-052.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-246](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-246.md) | In quantum theory, what does a failure of Kochen–Specker noncontextuality refute, as against a failure of Spekkens's generalized noncontextuality, and which of the two notions is broader? | The conceptual part of [QUESTION-067](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-067.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [THEORY-011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-011.md), [THEORY-015](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-015.md), [THEORY-016](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-016.md), [THEORY-231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-231.md) and [THEORY-559](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-559.md). A Kochen–Specker proof refutes measurement noncontextuality together with outcome determinism, and so universal generalized noncontextuality. A generalized no-go refutes a positive quasiprobability representation, and Leibnizian representations within classical realism. The generalized notion is strictly broader. | [QUESTION-247](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-247.md) | If the communicative object is a presheaf of propositions over a category of contexts, is the negation its topos logic gives an orthocomplement or a Heyting pseudo-complement, and what fixes it? | The conditional part of [QUESTION-055](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [THEORY-516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) and [THEORY-037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md). Over a presheaf of contexts the truth values are sieves, and negation is the Heyting pseudo-complement that the base category fixes, not an orthocomplement. Whether the communicative object is such a presheaf, over which base, and whether probes split it into sectors, stays with [QUESTION-055](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-248](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-248.md) | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), does a scalar linear coarse variable whose reduced dynamics carry memory admit an exact finite-dimensional Markovian augmentation? | [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) for the linear Gaussian class, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [CLAIM-398](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-398.md). Yes: a scalar coarse variable Y = LX of a VAR(1) on ℝⁿ is an ARMA process of orders at most (n, n − 1). Its Mori–Zwanzig memory is non-zero at every lag in general, but finitely many coordinates, built from Y's own past and innovations, carry it exactly. Other classes, error in terms of the eliminated spectrum, and the ruling on levels stay with [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-249](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-249.md) | If a map of a representation X of finite support keeps no information about a categorical concept A, how much information about X can it keep, and when does it keep that much? | The one-step, information-theoretic part of [QUESTION-010](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-010.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [THEORY-281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-281.md). The map can keep at most H(X\|A), and it keeps that much exactly when X is a function of the output and A. | [QUESTION-250](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-250.md) | Can a macro description of a known mechanism have interventional autonomy, an effective-information advantage over its micro description, without organizational closure or self-individuation? | The part of [QUESTION-093](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-093.md) that Hoel, Albantakis & Tononi settle, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered Yes by [THEORY-222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md).
